newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas crop planting advanced in past week.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas crop planting advanced in past week.

text.p: Corn, rice and sorghum planting progressed in Arkansas during the week ended Sunday before heavy rain arrived late in the week, according to the state's Agricultural Statistics Service.
Five days were suitable for fieldwork.
Corn was 42 percent planted versus 37 a year ago and the 38 five-year average.
Rice was seven percent planted versus one a year ago and the five percent average.
Sorghum was 11 percent planted versus five a year ago and six on average.
Winter wheat was 13 percent headed versus 13 a year ago and the four percent average. The crop was rated three percent excellent, 36 good, 39 fair, 19 poor and two very poor.
Oats were rated four percent good, 84 fair, and 12 poor.
Soil moisture was rated 25 percent surplus and 75 percent adequate.
